key_insight: Matrix product states avoid poor local minima because their gauge freedom creates effective local overparametrization, making their energy landscapes much easier to optimize than brickwork circuits.
engineering_relevance: This suggests sequential quantum circuit ansätze and tensor-network methods can be far more trainable for variational optimization than standard shallow brickwork circuits.
method: Proved the MPS energy landscape has no poor local minima under the studied setting.
Showed the local minimum distribution is invariant to moving the orthogonality center.
Compared sequential circuits against brickwork circuits on random Hamiltonians.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments in the abstract show sequential circuit optimization converges near the optimum even for random Hamiltonians, unlike brickwork circuits.
watch_item: The guarantee is specific to the MPS setting and the stated optimization framework, so it may not transfer directly to all variational quantum circuit architectures or hardware-constrained implementations.
paper_title: Absence of poor local minima in matrix product states
